rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lack of gratitude is expressed as disbelief in resurrection and denial of God's power to revive the dead.
rows.anchor: بين عدم شكرهم بإتيانهم بضده وهو الكفر وإنكار قدرته على إحياء الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction links this denial to their earlier claims that Muhammad was no messenger, God was not one, and resurrection was impossible.
rows.anchor: فإنهم قالوا محمد ليس برسول والله ليس بواحد وقالوا الحشر ليس بممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense describes rejection of the Prophet's mission arising during his lifetime, while the past tense for resurrection reflects an older denial inherited from their ancestors.
rows.anchor: تكذيبهم إياه في رسالته لم يكن قبل وجوده وإنما كان ذلك حالة وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text explicitly reports their denial of the Messenger and resurrection, but not of divine unity, because they acknowledged unity in principle despite outward claims.
rows.anchor: وأما الوحدانية فكانوا يعترفون بها في المعنى ، ألا ترى أن الله تعالى قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation of the human being proves God's ability to restore him; Razi links this proof to verses about bringing the dead back to life.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن خلق الإنسان ابتداء دليل على قدرته على إعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation of the heavens also proves that God can create people again, as the cited verses argue.
rows.anchor: وكذلك خلق السموات كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God should take the form of glorifying Him and declaring Him free of every evil; this is the intended sense of tasbih.
rows.anchor: فينبغي أن يكون ذكركم إياه على وجه التعظيم والتنزيه عن كل سوء وهو المراد بالتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation takes tasbih here to mean prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد منه الصلاة وقيل للصلاة تسبيحه بكرة وأصيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning morning and evening as the two endpoints implies continuous remembrance, since mentioning the endpoints can convey the whole interval.
rows.anchor: مريد العموم قد يذكر الطرفين ويفهم منهما الوسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates this rhetorical implication with the Prophet's mention of the first and last without the middle, which conveys comprehensive scope.
rows.anchor: كقوله عليه السلام ( لو أن أولكم وآخركم ) ولم يذكر وسطكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's prayer and mercy toward believers, while they fail to remember Him, is meant to encourage their remembrance and glorification.
rows.anchor: يعني هو يصلي عليكم ويرحمكم وأنتم لا تذكرونه فذكر صلاته تحريضا للمؤمنين على الذكر والتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings believers from darkness to light by guiding them through His mercy.
rows.anchor: يعني يهديكم برحمته والصلاة من الله رحمة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: A reported view, which Razi finds plausible, allows the shared word to carry both meanings: God's mercy and the angels' seeking forgiveness, including a word's literal and figurative senses together.
rows.anchor: اللفظ المشترك يجوز استعماله في معنييه معا وكذلك الجمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز في لفظ جائز وينسب هذا القول إلى الشافعي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy and seeking forgiveness share concern for the recipient; this common element is intended, so the wording indicates it by implication as part of both meanings.
rows.anchor: الرحمة والاستغفار يشتركان في العناية بحال المرحوم والمستغفر له والمراد هو القدر المشترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God merciful is glad tidings for all believers and shows that His prayer is not limited to those who heard the revelation directly.
rows.anchor: بشارة لجميع المؤمنين وإشارة إلى أن قوله { يصلى عليكم } غير مختص بالسامعين وقت الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan had no coercive authority over them; his influence was only a sign God created to disclose what He already knew would occur.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه ليس بملجىء وإنما هو آية ، وعلامة خلقها الله لتبيين ما هو في علمه السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have prevented Satan and knows what will happen; preserving something entails both knowledge and power, since an ignorant or incapable being cannot preserve it.
rows.anchor: فالحفظ يدخل في مفهومه العلم والقدرة ، إذ الجاهل بالشيء لا يمكنه حفظه ولا العاجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call on the alleged deities to remove harm is sarcastic; the passage then establishes that they own nothing.
rows.anchor: قل للمشركين ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دون الله ليكشفوا عنكم الضر على سبيل التهكم

rows.speaker: من يقول الله تعالى خلق السماء
rows.claim: One path to shirk posits God as creator and lord of heaven while people worship the stars and angels there as their own gods.
rows.anchor: قول من يقول الله تعالى خلق السماء والسماويات وجعل الأرض والأرضيات في حكمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the first doctrine, the alleged celestial gods own nothing in the heavens, as its adherents themselves concede, and nothing on earth, contrary to their claim.
rows.anchor: إنهم لا يملكون في السموات شيئا كما اعترفتم ، قال ولا في الأرض على خلاف ما زعمتم

rows.speaker: من يقول السموات من الله
rows.claim: A second doctrine assigns the heavens to God alone but makes earthly things His work through the planets, giving other beings a share in earthly creation.
rows.anchor: قول من يقول السموات من الله على سبيل الاستبداد والأرضيات منه ولكن بواسطة الكواكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against this doctrine, the earth belongs to God just as heaven does; no other being has any share in either.
rows.anchor: الأرض كالسماء لله لا لغيره ، ولا لغيره فيها نصيب

rows.speaker: من قال التركيبات والحوادث كلها من الله تعالى
rows.claim: A third doctrine says God created all compositions and events but delegated their execution to the planets, so the planets act as His agents.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : قول من قال : التركيبات والحوادث كلها من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against delegation, Razi analogizes a king's command to a servant's act, then denies that God delegated anything and affirms His complete watch over all things.
rows.anchor: ما فوض إلى شيء شيئا ، بل هو على كل شيء حفيظ ورقيب

rows.speaker: من قال إنا نعبد الأصنام
rows.claim: A fourth doctrine worships idols as images of angels in order to obtain their intercession.
rows.anchor: قول من قال إنا نعبد الأصنام التي هي صور الملائكة ليشفعوا لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession benefits only those God permits, so worshipping other beings for intercession is futile and forfeits the intercession sought.
rows.anchor: فلا فائدة لعبادتكم غير الله فإن الله لا يأذن في الشفاعة لمن يعبد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about fear being removed means that terror was taken away; Razi compares its form to saying that a camel was relieved of ticks and calls it an intensified removal.
rows.anchor: أي أزيل الفزع عنهم ، يقال قرد البعير إذا أخذ منه القراد ويقال لهذا تشديد السلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation places the fear at revelation: the heavens are frightened, then ask Gabriel what God said, and he answers that it was the truth, meaning revelation.
rows.anchor: الفزع الذي عند الوحي فإن الله عندما يوحي يفزع من في السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation makes the fear concern the Hour: Muhammad's mission is a sign of its approach, and after the fear abates the angels ask Gabriel, who answers that the truth is revelation.
rows.anchor: الفزع الذي من الساعة وذلك لأن الله تعالى لما أوحى إلى محمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation places the removal of fear at death: people acknowledge the truth then, which benefits those previously truthful and harms those previously opposed.
rows.anchor: هو أن الله تعالى يزيل الفزع وقت الموت عن القلوب فيعترف كل أحد بأن ما قال الله تعالى هو الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first two readings, hatta completes the command to warn until the audience hears the revelation; on the third, it completes the claim of disbelief until terror makes them abandon it.
rows.anchor: على القولين الأولين قوله تعالى : { حتى } غاية متعلقة بقوله تعالى : { قل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the revelation and Hour readings, angels ask Gabriel and angels answer; for the death reading, the polytheists ask the angels and the polytheists acknowledge the truth.
rows.anchor: وعلى القولين الأولين فاعل قوله تعالى : { قالوا ماذا } هو الملائكة السائلون من جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is what exists; because God's existence cannot be followed by nonexistence, He is absolutely true.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الحق هو الموجود ثم إن الله تعالى لما كان وجوده لا يرد عليه عدم كان حقا مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech is called true because its mental meaning relates to an external reality; falsehood either lacks a mental referent or holds a belief contrary to reality.
rows.anchor: والكلام الذي يكون صدقا يسمى حقا ، لأن الكلام له متعلق في الخارج بواسطة أنه متعلق بما في الذهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike deliberate falsehood, which lacks an external object from the outset, or conjecture, which later fails, God's speech is never invalidated.
rows.anchor: وكلام الله لا بطلان له في أول الأمر كما يكون كلام الكاذب المعاند ولا يأتيه الباطل كما يكون كلام الظان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being the Highest and Greatest means He exceeds every perfection absolutely; Razi argues this rules out bodily form or occupying a location, since either would make His height or greatness relative.
rows.anchor: وهذا يبطل القول بكونه جسما وفي حيز ، لأن كل من كان في حيز فإن العقل يحكم بأنه مشار إليه

none: Quran verse text only; no commentary point appears in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Gathering, God asks the angels whether the people worshipped them, as a humiliating challenge to those claiming to worship angels and planets.
rows.anchor: فيسأل الملائكة أهم كانوا يعبدونكما إهانة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' answer that God is their patron conveys that serving God is more fitting and beloved than having the foolish as one's worshippers; Razi illustrates this with the madman who prefers followers among flies and worms to serving a great king.
rows.anchor: يعني كونك ولينا بالمعبودية أولى ، وأحب إلينا من كونهم أولياءنا بالعبادة لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels say people worshipped the jinn by obeying their commands; the angels merely served as the direction toward which people turned, since worship means obedience.
rows.anchor: أي كانوا ينقادون لأمر الجن ، فهم في الحقيقة كانوا يعبدون الجن ، ونحن كنا كالقبلة لهم ، لأن العبادة هي الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels may say most people believed in the jinn to avoid claiming exhaustive knowledge: those they had seen and observed did so, while others may have escaped their notice.
rows.anchor: أن الملائكة احترزوا عن دعوى الإحاطة بهم فقالوا أكثرهم لأن الذين رأوهم واطلعوا على أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the angels distinguish observable outward worship from inward belief, since only God knows what hearts contain.
rows.anchor: العبادة عمل ظاهر والإيمان عمل باطن فقالوا : { بل كانوا يعبدون الجن } لاطلاعهم على أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reconciliation is that the command to warn is general regardless of its effect, while effective warning reaches only those who follow the Reminder and fear God.
rows.anchor: قوله : { لتنذر } أي كيفما كان سواء كان مفيدا أو لم يكن وقوله : { إنما تنذر } أي الإنذار المفيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reconciliation is to warn everyone because the Prophet cannot know whom he will guide, while the intended beneficiaries are those who respond; even the stubborn are not the only audience.
rows.anchor: فأنذر على سبيل العموم وإنما تنذر بذلك الإنذار العام من يتبع الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reconciliation makes the warning general at first; after the Prophet has fully delivered it and some mock, turn away, or act arrogantly, only followers remain receptive to warning.
rows.anchor: قوله : { لتنذر } أي أولا فإذا أنذرت وبالغت وبلغت واستهزأ البعض وتولى واستكبر وولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A closely related view distinguishes levels: warn everyone about foundational beliefs, but warn followers of the Reminder about practical duties such as prayer and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: إنك تنذر الكل بالأصول ، وإنما تنذر بالفروع من ترك الصلاة والزكاة من اتبع الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Reminder may mean following the Quran itself, the Quran's signs, or demonstrative proof that completes innate nature; on each reading the warned are learned people who fear God.
rows.anchor: من اتبع القرآن الثاني : من اتبع ما في القرآن من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Reminder means faith and fearing the Merciful means righteous action; forgiveness corresponds to faith and the noble reward to deeds.
rows.anchor: قوله : { اتبع الذكر } أي آمن ، وقوله : { وخشى الرحمان } أي عمل صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in Reminder supports identifying it as the Quran already mentioned as the Wise Quran.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الذكر بالقرآن يتأيد بتعريف الذكر بالألف واللام ، وقد تقدم ذكر القرآن في قوله تعالى : { والقرءان الحكيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although mercy tends to produce hope and reliance, the wise should still fear the Merciful, whose repeated gifts make the prospect of their withdrawal weighty.
rows.anchor: وهي أن الرحمة تورث الاتكال والرجاء فقال مع أنه رحمن ورحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah and al-Rahman are described as two names particular to God: Allah conveys awe and al-Rahman affection, so one should fear Him without despair and hope in Him without feeling safe.
rows.anchor: فالله اسم ينبىء عن الهيبة والرحمن ينبىء عن العاطفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear in the unseen can mean fear based on evidence before matters become visible, when fear would no longer serve a purpose.
rows.anchor: يعني بالدليل وإن لم ينته إلى درجة المرئي المشاهد فإن عند الانتهاء إلى تلك الدرجة لا يبقى للخشية فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common interpretation of fearing God in the unseen is fear concerning the unseen realities of the Resurrection; another view includes divine unity.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أن المراد بالغيب ما غاب عنا وهو أحوال القيامة ، وقيل إن الوحدانية تدخل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of good news signals the second part of the Messenger's task after warning; those who benefit from warning should also receive glad tidings.
rows.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى الأمر الثاني من أمري الرسالة فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بشير ونذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite forgiveness signifies an immense forgiveness that covers every side, leaving no trace of the lower self and revealing the lights of the purified spirit.
rows.anchor: على التنكير أي بمغفرة واسعة تستر من جميع الجوانب حتى لا يرى عليه أثر من آثار النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noble reward is a reward characterized by generosity; Razi points back to his prior explanations of noble provision.
rows.anchor: أي ذي كرم ، وقد ذكرنا ما في الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes salam an appositive explaining what the people of Paradise desire; it is semantically like a nominal sentence with a prepositional predicate, though grammatically parsed as apposition.
rows.anchor: هو بدل مما يدعون كأنه تعالى لما قال : { لهم ما * يدعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the first parsing; on it, ma may instead be an indefinite thing they desire, then specified by salam as an appositive.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الصحيح وثانيها سلام خبر ما ولهم لبيان الجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes salam the predicate of ma, with lahum marking the beneficiaries; salam means that their desired things are safe, pure, or sound for them.
rows.anchor: سلام خبر ما ولهم لبيان الجهة تقديره ما يدعون سالم لهم أي خالص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third, novel and good parsing treats salam as a separate nominal sentence with an omitted predicate, meaning Peace be upon them; it may be God's present address to them.
rows.anchor: وهذا وجه مبتكر جيد ما يدل عليه منقول ، أو نقول تقديره سلام عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the separate-sentence parsing, the shift from describing what they receive to directly saying Peace be upon you is a form of grammatical address shift.
rows.anchor: ويكون هذا نوعا من الالتفات حيث قال لهم كذا وكذا ، ثم قال سلام عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawlan may be an accusative verbal noun: God or the angels say the greeting, God states it as speech, or He promises that their wishes are safely granted.
rows.anchor: نصب على المصدر تقديره على قولنا المراد لهم سلام هو أن يقال لهم سلام يقوله الله قولا أو تقوله الملائكة قولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects parsing qawlan as a specification distinguishing a spoken greeting from a performed one, because this grammatical construction is categorically invalid.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال على هذا إنه تمييز لأن السلام قد يكون قولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting comes from a merciful Lord, whereas the other honor is provision at arrival from a forgiving Lord; initial hospitality signals honor but does not guarantee later treatment.
rows.anchor: أما هناك فلأن النزل ما يرزق النزيل أولا ، وذلك وإن كان يدل عليه ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiving reassures the servant about past deeds, since receiving food does not preclude later punishment; the greeting instead shows the honor of the person addressed, an especially striking kindness from his Lord.
rows.anchor: والسلام يظهر مزية تعظيمه للمسلم عليه لا بمغفرة فقال : { رب * غفور } لأن رب الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant answers the excuse that human ignorance is a defense: God warned people by clarifying the way through messengers and explaining what they should and should not do.
rows.anchor: والجهل من الأعذار ، فقال الله ذلك عند عدم الإنذار ، وقد سبق إيضاح السبل بإيضاح الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi records four linguistic forms: kasra on the hamza of aʿhad; kasra on its hā, on the daraba-yadribu pattern; changing ʿayn to jīm before hā; and then assimilating hā into ḥā.
rows.anchor: الأولى : كسر همزة إعهد وحروف الاستقبال كلها تكسر إلا الياء فلا يقال يعلم ويعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hā may take kasra on the daraba-yadribu pattern.
rows.anchor: الثانية : كسر الهاء من باب ضرب يضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dialect changes ʿayn to jīm whenever ʿayn is followed by hā, yielding a form like ajhad.
rows.anchor: الثالثة : قلب العين جيما ألم أجهد وذلك في كل عين بعدها هاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After that sound change, hā may assimilate into ḥā, yielding aḥad; Razi cites the heard phrase daḥā'a maḥā' as an example.
rows.anchor: الرابعة : إدغام الهاء في الحاء بعد القلب فيقال ألم أحد ، وقد سمع قوم يقولون دحاء محا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closest meaning of aʿhad is Did I enjoin or instruct you?.
rows.anchor: أقربها وأقربها ألم أوص إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the covenant as the one made with Adam, cited in the command to Adam in Ta-Ha.
rows.anchor: أنه هو العهد الذي كان مع أبينا آدم بقوله : { وعهدنا إلى * ءادم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view identifies it as the covenant with Adam's descendants, whose acknowledgment of God entails worshipping no one else.
rows.anchor: أنه هو الذي كان مع ذرية آدم بقوله تعالى : { ألست بربكم قالوا بلى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the strongest view that every people received this covenant through a Messenger; this explains the rational consensus that Satan commands evil despite disagreement about its nature and manner.
rows.anchor: هو الأقوى ، أن ذلك كان مع كل قوم على لسان رسول ، ولذلك اتفق العقلاء على أن الشيطان يأمر بالشر
